summary: Discovery-focused POC scoping to decide between Redwood hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment. Customer needs: sub-100ms p50 for short assistant queries, batch embedding pipeline for search indexing, monthly volume ~120M tokens with peak 250 rps, strict data residency and KMS requirements. Discussed benchmarks, success metrics (latency, cost per 1M tokens, fidelity), timeline for a 4-week pilot and security review. Agreed next steps: share sample workload, Redwood to run short hosted benchmark and provide dedicated sizing + cost estimate.
header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Taylor Reed (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel (CTO - Skyward Bio), Alex Guerrero (Head of ML), Samir Khan (Infrastructure Lead), Olivia Chen (Security)
Recording: available in CRM
transcript:
[00:00] Taylor Reed: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Taylor from Redwood Inference, Jordan's here on the engineering side. quick agenda — scope the POC, success criteria, sizing, security constraints.
[00:18] Dr. Maya Patel: Thanks, yeah we wanted to get this scoped quickly. we have two main use cases: in-app assistant for researchers (low latency) and nightly embedding pipeline for indexing our internal docs.
[00:32] Jordan Kim: Great — can you give ballpark traffic? tokens per month, peak rps, typical prompt lengths?
[00:40] Alex Guerrero: Sure, rough numbers: about 120 million tokens/month total, average prompt+response 150 tokens, but assistant queries are shorter ~40-60 tokens. Peak concurrent request rate around 200-300 rps during workday spikes. embedding jobs run as batch overnight, roughly 5k docs per night, 768-dim embeddings.
[01:05] Samir Khan: On infra/security — we need SOC2, SSO + SAML, audit logs, and key control. If we go private we may need HSM-backed KMS. Also residency: data must remain in EU and US zones, depending on dataset.
[01:25] Taylor Reed: Understood. For decision criteria we'll typically look at latency targets, unit cost, and compliance. Hosted is fastest to iterate; Dedicated gives predictable throughput/cost; Private for strict control and air-gap.
[01:40] Olivia Chen: For compliance, encryption at rest + in-transit, customer-managed keys, audit trail, and annual penetration test reports are must-haves.
[01:52] Jordan Kim: Quick note on latencies — for the assistant use case are you targeting p50 or p95?
[01:58] Alex Guerrero: p50 under 100ms ideally, p95 under 300ms. We can accept slightly higher for longer context, but the researcher experience must feel instant.
[02:12] Taylor Reed: That is helpful. For 100ms p50 on short sequences we can often hit that on hosted with optimized kernels and batching turned off for those routes. Dedicated helps if you need sustained 300 rps at low tail latencies. Private can match but depends on your on-prem GPU type and networking.
[02:30] Dr. Maya Patel: Cost is also big — our finance will want a cost per 1M tokens and an estimated monthly run-rate. Dedicated commit or annual reserved looks appealing if the numbers make sense.
[02:42] Jordan Kim: On benchmarks: Jordan suggests we run two short benchmarks — one hosted run using your redacted prompt set to get real p50/p95 and cost per token, and a dedicated sizing estimate based on throughput model (we can simulate with synthetic load).
[02:56] Alex Guerrero: How intrusive is the hosted benchmark? We can't share PHI; will redaction be okay?
[03:02] Taylor Reed: Yes, redacted/pseudonymized samples are fine; we just need representative tokens and prompt families. We'll sign an NDA if needed.
[03:12] Samir Khan: Network — if hosted, traffic must egress to Redwood cloud; are there IP allowlists and VPC peering options?
[03:20] Jordan Kim: We support IP allowlists, private peering for Dedicated, and VPC connectors for Private deployments. For hosted we can also configure VPC egress with partners but typically data flows to Redwood-managed infra.
[03:34] Olivia Chen: About KMS — we require customer-managed keys and audit logs. Is that supported on hosted?
[03:40] Taylor Reed: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations on Dedicated and Private; hosted supports envelope encryption with customer KMS in some regions — we'll confirm specifics in the security call.
[03:52] Alex Guerrero: For embeddings, do you support batching and async? We want throughput overnight and cost matters more than latency there.
[03:59] Jordan Kim: Yes embeddings are batch-friendly; we can do high-throughput vectorization with automatic batching and quantized models to lower cost. We'll capture your doc size distribution to propose optimal batch sizes.
[04:16] Dr. Maya Patel: How do you handle model upgrades and rollouts? We want canarying and quick rollback for any quality regression.
[04:24] Taylor Reed: Redwood has rollout policies — canary percentages, A/B, automatic fallback to previous compatible model variant if quality drops. We'll show examples in the console demo.
[04:36] Alex Guerrero: Regarding models — are you recommending an open model or commercial one? Cost vs quality tradeoff matters; we prefer an open variant if fidelity is similar.
[04:46] Jordan Kim: We'll benchmark a 1B-3B family quantized variant and a 7B variant to compare latency/quality/cost. For embeddings we'll use a dense 768 model; we can test open alternatives as well.
[04:59] Samir Khan: Autoscaling — for dedicated pools how does burst capacity work? during spikes we don't want throttling.
[05:07] Taylor Reed: Dedicated supports configurable autoscale policies and a burst buffer to reduce throttling risk. SLOs can be defined per-route.
[05:16] Olivia Chen: Audit logs and retention — can you retain detailed logs for 12 months? That's our baseline for compliance.
[05:23] Jordan Kim: Yes, with an add-on plan we can retain request-level logs for up to 12 months and provide log export to your SIEM. We'll outline options in the security packet.
[05:34] Alex Guerrero: Timeline — if we start now what's realistic for a POC? We want benchmarks, decision, and maybe start pilot in 4 weeks.
[05:42] Taylor Reed: Typical POC: week 0 share data and success criteria; week 1 hosted benchmark + initial results; week 2 dedicated sizing and cost estimate; week 3 security review; week 4 finalize pilot plan and contract. So 4 weeks is feasible.
[05:58] Dr. Maya Patel: Acceptance criteria — what do we put as success metrics? I'd propose: assistant p50 <100ms, p95 <300ms, embedding throughput >= target nightly ingestion time (6 hours), cost per 1M tokens below threshold X, and no unresolved critical security items.
[06:16] Taylor Reed: That's a good list. We'll convert into measurable SLOs and include in the POC doc.
[06:24] Jordan Kim: For the hosted benchmark we'll measure p50/p95 for your three prompt families, throughput on synthetic peak load, and cost breakdown (compute vs model). We'll also surface recommendations for quantization and batching to meet cost targets.
[06:39] Alex Guerrero: If hosted results show acceptable latency but costs are high, how easy is it to migrate to dedicated?
[06:46] Taylor Reed: Migration is straightforward — same API, you pin model versions and route to Dedicated capacity. We'll provide a migration runbook and a short trial of dedicated sizing if needed.
[06:55] Samir Khan: For Private, what are the minimum hardware requirements? We might prefer private for EU data residency.
[07:02] Jordan Kim: Minimums depend on model — for a quantized 7B you might need 4xA100 or equivalent, but Private options can be tuned. We'll provide a recommended spec based on the benchmark results.
[07:12] Olivia Chen: Are there any known gaps on compliance we should flag now? e.g., pen test frequency, ISO27001?
[07:18] Taylor Reed: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO-related docs; pen test cadence varies by plan but enterprise customers can request annual tests and provide reports. We'll include those artifacts in the security packet.
[07:30] Alex Guerrero: One more question on logging: can we redact PII before logs are stored? We need to ensure logs don't persist PHI.
[07:38] Jordan Kim: Yes, we can configure redaction and minimal logging for sensitive routes. That will be part of the security configuration.
[07:48] Dr. Maya Patel: Ok let's talk concrete next steps — we'll share three representative prompt families and the embedding sample. Also need pricing scenarios for hosted vs 3-year dedicated commit.
[07:59] Taylor Reed: Great. Jordan will run the hosted benchmark once we receive data; I'll follow up with pricing. We'll also schedule the security deep-dive with Olivia.
[08:08] Olivia Chen: Good. Also, please include network diagrams and data flow for hosted option so we can share with our infra team.
[08:16] Taylor Reed: Absolutely. We'll send an initial POC doc today and a security packet by early next week.
[08:24] Alex Guerrero: Timeline check — can you get preliminary hosted numbers by Friday?
[08:28] Jordan Kim: If you share data by Wednesday we can run a hosted quick-run and surface initial numbers by Friday.
[08:34] Alex Guerrero: Okay we'll aim to send by Wednesday.
[08:38] Dr. Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. One small note — sometimes Fireflies transcripts mangle technical terms, so apologies if anything sounds off in the recording.
[08:48] Taylor Reed: Not a problem. Appreciate the time. We'll recap next steps in email.
[08:53] Meeting end: 15:55 UTC
